correctness.rationale: For r=0,1,2,3 favoured incidences at a cubic vertex, minimal monochromatic incident pairs are (1,0,1,3). The three affine inequalities f(r)>=1-r, r-1 and 2r-3 imply F>=max(10-2k,2k-10,4k-30). At k=5 Petersen is non-three-edge-colourable because every perfect matching has odd-cycle complement, and one defect is impossible by parity of total incidences, giving m_5>=2. Sixteen explicit witness strings attain the bounds. The 16 multiplicities in the package were independently regenerated by an original C++17 depth-first ternary enumeration with a different Petersen edge order and all 14,348,907 labelled states, not just rerunning the original verifier. Every m_k,g_k matches; the 900 balanced and 900 (4,5,6) zero-field types match. Direct lower envelope at x=-2,0,2,4 yields exactly sectors and counts 17022,1800,11652,3123; off crossings 1782,300,300,192,1. Valid for every J>0,h real, fixed 15-site graph; enumeration is an exhaustive finite proof here, not an infinite-family assertion.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is the canonical smallest cubic snark; its 3-state Potts model on the line graph naturally relaxes edge three-colouring by counting conflicting incident pairs. The complete exact occupancy-dependent ground-state table provides a non-implied frustration benchmark with a physically interpretable singular zero-field choice between four and six favoured sites, unlike defect-free class-I cubic graphs. The exact coexistence degeneracies and 900+900 structural split can inform future tests of graph-colouring/spin models on frustrated finite clusters. This is a motivated natural finite invariant, with no claim to a thermodynamic limit or novel general partition-function formula.
